supersedes: multiagent.json (B3), withdrawn 2026-10-24: its weight updates were monotone by construction, so the realized lifetime could not fall below the bound and measured only the construction.
context: Registered simulation of learning trading agents in the cohort economy of Definition def:cohort, checking Corollary thm:lifetime and asking whether the lifetime bound is informative when agents learn from their own profits.
rule: phi_i(y)=tanh(y) for every cohort (sector bound s_i=1)

shocks.adversarial: w_{t+1}=wbar*sign(x_t) (sign(0)=+1) with probability p_adv, else Uniform[-wbar,wbar]

primary_1: Implementation check (guaranteed by Corollary thm:lifetime, reported as a check, not as evidence): in every one of the 200 runs, max_{t<=T_valid}|x_t| <= Z_budget, max_{t<=T_valid} sum_i|q_i(t)|s_i <= Phi_max, and every weight step is at most gamma.
primary_2: Informative: in the adversarial regime (100 runs pooled over the four learning rates), the first time total sensitivity exceeds Phi_max is at most 3*T_valid in at least 50% of runs.
correction: P1 is a deterministic check and carries no error rate; P2 is the only inferential primary, so no multiplicity correction is applied.
descriptive: distribution of T_cross/T_valid and T_breach/T_valid by regime and learning rate
development: The runner was smoke-tested on development seed 1 with one repetition and horizon multiple 1; no outcome was printed or inspected.
opening_rule: The specification, its hash and an unlock counter at 0 are committed and pushed to origin/main in a commit of their own. The runner refuses to start unless the committed specification matches origin/main and the counter is 0; it sets the counter to 1 and runs once.
